k1.text: Night of 1–2 May 2011 — Jalalabad, Afghanistan to Abbottabad, Pakistan

k2.text: Two Ghosthawks — modified stealth helicopters — lift off from Jalalabad with about two dozen SEALs, an interpreter and a dog, Cairo

k3.text: Backup Chinooks carrying a quick-reaction force wait about two-thirds of the way to Abbottabad

k4.text: An MQ-9 Reaper circles above Abbottabad, streaming live video

k5.text: The flight from Jalalabad takes about 90 minutes

k6.text: Ghosthawk 1 hovers over the high-walled yard, loses lift and hard-lands

k7.text: At the guest house, the courier Abu Ahmed al-Kuwaiti opens fire and is killed

k8.text: Teams breach the inner gate while Chalk 2 sets a cordon on the street outside

k9.text: Ground floor of the main house: Abrar al-Kuwaiti and his wife Bushra are killed

k10.text: On the stairs, bin Laden's son Khalid is killed

k11.text: Third floor: Osama bin Laden, unarmed, is killed — "Geronimo, EKIA" is relayed back

k12.text: Operators collect computers, drives and documents; women and children are moved to safety in the yard

k13.text: A backup Chinook is called in to replace the damaged Ghosthawk

k14.text: Before leaving, the team destroys the damaged Ghosthawk to protect its technology

k14b.text: Before leaving, the team destroys the damaged Ghosthawk to protect its technology

k15.text: Roughly 38 minutes on target. The force returns to Jalalabad with no American casualties

k17.text: The morning after, a satellite captures the aftermath on Google Earth
